cards.title: Introduction to Error Handling
cards.content:
When building web applications with Flask, things can and will go wrong. Unhandled exceptions result in generic 500 Internal Server Errors, which provide a poor user experience.

Proper error handling ensures your app fails gracefully, logs errors for debugging, and returns meaningful HTTP status codes and responses to the client.

cards.title: Match HTTP Status Codes to Meanings
Using Flask's abort()
cards.content:
To abort request handling and return an error code immediately, Flask provides the abort() function.

from flask import abort, render_template

@app.route('/user/<int:user_id>')
def get_user(user_id):
    user = load_user(user_id)
    if not user:
        abort(404)
    return render_template('user.html', user=user)

content.question: What happens when abort(404) is called inside a Flask view function?

options.text: Flask raises a Python exception and immediately stops executing the rest of the view function.
Flask redirects the user to the homepage.
Flask ignores it unless a try-catch block is used.
Flask shuts down the development server.

cards.title: Custom Error Pages with @app.errorhandler
cards.content:
You can create custom error pages using the @app.errorhandler decorator. This allows you to catch specific HTTP status codes or Python exceptions.

@app.errorhandler(404)
def page_not_found(error):
    return render_template('404.html'), 404

@app.errorhandler(500)
def internal_server_error(error):
    return render_template('500.html'), 500

Always remember to return the appropriate status code integer as the second return value!

cards.title: Handling Custom Exceptions
cards.content:
Flask also allows you to register error handlers for custom Python exception classes you define in your application.

class InvalidAPIUsage(Exception):
    status_code = 400

    def __init__(self, message, status_code=None, payload=None):
        super().__init__()
        self.message = message
        if status_code is not None:
            self.status_code = status_code
        self.payload = payload

@app.errorhandler(InvalidAPIUsage)
def handle_invalid_usage(error):
    response = jsonify(error.to_dict())
    response.status_code = error.status_code
    return response

cards.title: Order the Error Handling Setup Steps

items.text: Define a custom exception class or identify the HTTP error code.
Create a view function to handle the error and render a template or JSON.
Test the error response by triggering the exception in development.
